Microwave Resonator Spectroscopy of Wafer-Scale
Magnesium Diboride

Author: Albert Wandui, JPL Postdoctoral Fellow (365H)
Jason Allmaras (365H), Jon Greenfield (365H), Matt Kenyon (365H), Cliff Frez (365K), Sahil Patel
(365H), Daniel Shanks (365F), Matt Shaw (365H), Emma Wollman (365H), Daniel Cunnane (365H)

Background and Scientific Goals

Our objective is to develop and mature wafer-scale thin-film Magnesium Diboride (MgB2) enabling:

  • High performance superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) operating above 4K.
  • Superconducting filters and detectors for astrophysics and remote sensing in the sub-mm to far-IR regime.

This requires an accurate model of the both the equilibrium and non-equilibrium superconductivity and quasiparticle dynamics in a two-gap superconductor with various degrees of disorder and interband interaction strength.

Approach and Results I: Resonator Measurements

  • Extract the complex conductivity of films from measurements of the temperature (100mK - 30K),and frequency (100 MHz – 5 GHz) dependence of the resonance frequency and internal quality factor of MgB2

  • Noise measurements shed light on the quasiparticle dynamics in the superconducting film.

Outlook

  • Have developed a robust model of the 2-gap interaction in MgB2 applicable to films over a wide thickness, sheet resistance and Tc range.
  • Currently incorporating data from critical field measurements to constrain the total DOS.
  • Film-to-film comparisons can now inform fabrication and further work on modeling detector response.

Why MgB2?

Superconductivity in MgB2 is mediated by the electron-phonon interaction. Uniquely among BCS superconductors, it exhibits:

  • 2 interacting superconducting band gaps: a strongly coupled 2D π band and a weakly coupled 3d σ band.
  • The resulting high superconducting transition temperature Tc offers a compelling pathway for superconducting devices that operate at elevated temperatures or at higher frequencies.

JPL has developed a process for wafer-scale MgB2 with low roughness and high uniformity with Tc of up to 31 K for bulk films and high kinetic inductance [1,2].

Approach and Results II: Modeling 2 gap physics

  • Obtain the temperature dependent gap energies Δπ(T) and Δσ(T) and the band interaction parameters Vππ, Vπσ, Vσσ.
  • To do so, we developed a self-consistent approach to fitting the measured penetration depth using Eliashberg Theory.
$\sum_{\beta}\left(V_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}-N_{\alpha}\cdot\Pi_{\alpha}\cdot\delta_{\alpha\beta}\right)\cdot\Delta_{\beta}=0$
$\Pi_{\alpha}\;=\;\int\limits_{0}^{\omega_c}\mathrm{d}\xi\,\dfrac{\tanh[\beta\sqrt{\xi^{2}+|\Delta_{\alpha}|^{2}}/2]}{\sqrt{\xi^{2}+|\Delta_{\alpha}|^{2}}}$
  • Using 3 fit parameters: ratio of the DOS, ratio of the gap energies at T=0, and fraction of conductivity from the π band, we accurately reproduce both the penetration depth and the dissipation as a function of temperature [3].
